Reprography Unit, BIS, New Delhi. India

FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the 
draft finalized by the Industrial Trucks Sectional Committee had been approved by the Transport 
Engineering Division Council. 

This standard was first published in 1973. The revision of this standard has been taken up to 
align it with ISO/DIS ^184 'Reach and straddle forklift trucks — Stability tests', issued by the 
International Organization for Standardization ( ISO). This revision includes safety precautions 
to be adopted to prevent overturning of the truck while testing. 

In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final 
value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
'Rules for rounding off numerical values {revised). 



IS 7309 : 1993 



Indian Standard 



REACH AND STRADDLE FORKLIFT 
TRUCKS — METHOD OF STABILITY TESTS 

( First Revision ) 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard specifics the basic tests lor 
verification of the stability reach (retractable mast 
or fork) and straddle type of forklilt trucks that are 
pedestrian and rider-controlled. 

1.2 It also applies to pedestrian and rider-controlled 
reach (retractable mast or fork) forklift trucks and 
straddle forklift trucks with lilting or non-tilting masts 
or fork arms of rated capacity up to and including 
5 000 kg. It also applies to trucks operating under 
the same conditioas when equipped with load handling 
attachments. 

1.3 This standard does not apply to trucks when used 
as mobile cranes, or when handling suspended and 
free swinging loads. 

2 REFERKNC ICS 

The following Indian Standards arc necessary adjuncts 
to this standard:

3 TERMINOLOGY 

For the purpose of this standard, the terms and 
definitions as given in IS 4660 : 1977 shall apply. 

4 CONDITIONS OF VALIDITY 

4.1 Normal Operating (Conditions 

The basic tests specified in this standard ensure that 
the type of forklift truck under consideration has 
satisfactory stability when used reasonably and 
appropriately under normal operating conditions, 
which include: 

a) Stacking with the mast approximately vertical 
and the arms reasonably horizontal on 
substantially firm, smooth, level and prepared 
surfaces; 



b) Travelling with the mast or fork arms lilted 
rearwards and the load in the lowered 
( travelling ) ptxsition on substantially firm, 
smooth and prepared surfaces; 

c) 0|x-rating with the load centre of gravity on 
the off-set within 1(K) mm from the 
longitudinal centre plane of the truck. 

4.2 Operating Conditions Other than Nornial 

When the operating conditions differ from those 
stated in 4.1, one of the following shall be used 
for tests: 

a) a truck complying with Indian Slandard(s) 
covering different conditions; or 

b) a truck, the |X"rformance stability of which 
is agreed upon Ix-tween the manufacturers 
and the purchasers. This agreed |X-rfor- 
mance, however, shall not Ix less than Ihal 
required by the tests sjxcified for normal 
operating conditions (see 4.1 ). 

5 SIABILITY TESTS 

5.1 General Requirements 

5.1.1 Preparation for Tests 

5.1.1.1 The stability of these trucks shall be verified 
by means of the tests dcscrilxd Ih-Iow, using a tillable 
test platform. 

5.1.1.2 The test shall Ix carried oul on an 0|X'rational 
Inick. 

5.1.1.3 The ojxrator on rider-controlled trucks shall 
he represented by an objecl with a weight of 
90 kg, the stability during a lesl is thereby decreased. 
For a truck with a standing operator, an object with 
a weight of 90 kg shall Ix secured with its Centre 
of Gravity 1 (XK) mmatK)ve the tloorof the operator's 
platform at the centre of the position normally 
occupied by the operator. For a truck with a seated 
operator, the Centre of Gravity of the objecl shall 
be secured 150 mm above the Seal Index Point ( SIP ) 
as detennined in accordance with IS 11113 : 19S5, 
with the set at the mid-point of the adjustments 
provided. 

5.1.1.4 Fuel tanks of Internal Combustion engine 
trucks shall be full if stability is reduced. All other 



IS 73()9 : 1993 



tanks shall be lillcd to ihcir correct operating levels, 
where applicable. 

5,1.1.5 Tyres shall Ik" inttated to the pressures 
specified by the inick inanufacturer. Where tyre 
ballast is incorporated in the truck design, the use 
of ballast shall be in accordance with the 
manufacturer's instructions. 

5.2 Test Ix)ad 

5.2.1 rhe test load shall have a mass equivalent 
to the maximum ( rated ) load, Q, which the truck 
can elevate to its maximum lift height acting through 
the Centre of Gravity, G, normally positioned at the 
normal load centre distance, D, both hori/ontally 
from the front face of the fork arm shank and 
vertically from the upper face of the fork arm blade. 
This is indicated on the information plate fixed on 
the truck. 

5.2.2 When additional lift heights, loads and load 
centre distances are to be indicated on the informa- 
tion plate, the truck shall meet the requirements 
established by the lest specified in this standard for 
these additional ratings. 

5.2.3 For tests No. I, 2, 3 and 6, the Centre of 
Gravity, C, of the test load ( see Fig. 1 ) shall be 
located in the longitudinal centre plane AB of the 
truck. 




Fici. 1 PosrnoN of Ci-ntrk of GRAvrrv 

5.2.4 For reach and straddle forklifl trucks up to 
5 (XK) kg capacity, the normal load centre distance 
shall be as follows: 

a) 400 mm for loads up to 999 kg, 

b) 500 mm for loads of 1 000 kg and up to 
4 999 kg, and 

c) 600 mm for load of 5 000 kg and up to 
10 000 kg. 



5.2.5 Precautions shall be taken to prevent the 
overturning of the truck of displacement of the test 
load during the course of the tests. If the mcaiLs 
for preventing the total overturning of the truck 
consists of lashing or chaining, this shall Ik sufficiently 
slack to impose no appreciable restriction on the 
truck until the overturning point is reached. 

5.2.6 For tests No. 1, 3 and 6 the test load shall 
be cither ( see Table 1 ): 

a) firmly secured to the load carrier or equivalent 
structure; or 

b) susjXMided near the ground from an appropriate 
sup|x>rt placed on the forks such that the 
suspension point is at the point where the 
centre of gravity, G, of the test load would 
be located if the lest load were to be placed 
on the fork. 

5.3 l^K'ation of Truck on the Test Platform 

The initial position of the truck on the test platform 
shall be maintained during each test. 

5.3.1 This may be achieved by application of jwrking 
or service brakes, which can be secured in the 'on' 
position, or by wedging the wheels against the truck 
frame, ensuring however that articulation is not 
affected. 

5.3.2 Blocks/chocks having a maximum height 
not exceeding the value indicated in Table 2 
may be used, if necessary, to maintain the initial 
position of the truck on the test platform. Blocks 
or chocks, if used, shall not artificially improve 
stability. 

5.3.3 The coefficient of friction of the platform 
surface may Ik increased, if necessary, by an 
appropriate friction-increasing material. 

5.4 Verification of Vertical Position of Fork Arm 
Shank Front Face 

5.4.1 Before proceeding with test No. 1, the verti- 
cality of the front face of the fork arm shank or 
equivalent surface shall be verified by means of a 
plumb line or other suitable equipment. 

5.4.2 Elevate the fork and set the test load to 
approximately 300 mm above the test platform and 
with the front face of the fork arm shank vertical, 
establish a point, E ( see Fig. 2 ) on the fork arms 
or fork carrier having a fixed relationship to the 
Centre of Gravity of the test load, G. This point 
E shall be used to provide a reference datum, F, 
on the test platform. When the mast is elevated, a 
new point, F , on the test platform may occur ( see 
Fig. 3 ), and by the adjustments descril>cd below 
this new point F^ shall be returned to the original 
location of F ( see Fig. 4 )

5.4.3 For trucks with tillable masts, changes in the 
location of F, shall be corrected by varying the tilt 
of the mast or by retracting the mast or the fork 
arms within the limits of the truck design. 

5.4.4 For trucks with non-tiltable masts, adjustments 
in the fork arms or fork carrier tilt ( where provided ) 
or by retracting the mast may be used to correct 



for changes in location of point F^ within the limits 
of tilt of the truck design. 

5.5 Lift Height for Tests Simulating Travel 

For tests simulating travelling, that is tests No. 2, 
5 and 8, the upper face of the fork amis, measured 
at the heel of the fork arms, shall be positioned 
approximately 300 mm from the test platform.

5.6 Conditions for ('arrying Out the Test 

5.6.1 Position of the Truck on the Platform 

5.6.2 For tests No. 1 and 2, the truck shall be placed 
on the lest platform with the drive ( steer ) axle and 
the axle of the outrigger wheels parallel to the 
tilt axis, XY, of the test platform ( see Fig. 5 
to 8). 



5.6.3 For test No. 3, 4 and 5, the truck shall be 
placed on the test platform with line, MN, parallel 
to the tilt axis, XY, of the test platform ( see 
Fig. 9 to 16 ). 

5.6.4 For tests No. 6, 7 and 8, the truck shall Iv 
placed on the test platforn> with the longitudinal axis 
of the truck at right angles to the tilt axis XY of 
the platform ( sec Fig. 19 and 20 ). 

5.6.5 In the case of Fig. 13, the stccrable wheel nearest 
to the tin axis shall be parallel to it. Posilioas of 
steerable wheels on other designs are shown in 
Fig. 11, 12, 14, 15 and 16.

to 16). 

5.6.6 In the following figures, point M is defined 
as follows: 

a) For trucks with a single non-articulating drive 
(steer) wheel {see Fig. 11 ) — It is the 
vertical projection on the test platform of 
the jwinl of intersection between the centre- 
line of the drive ( steer ) axle and the centre- 
line of the drive wheel width. 

b) For trucks with a dual non-sprung castor 
wheel ( see Fig. 12 ) — It is the vertical 
projection on the test platform of the jwint 
of intersection between the centreline of the 



castor wheel axle and the mid-point between 
the two castor wheels; the non-sprung castor 
being positioned with the centreline of the 
castor wheel axle nearer to the centre plane 
of the truck. 

c) For trucks with a drive-steer axle in an 
articulating frame articulated in the centre 
plane (»f the truck ( see Fig. 13 ) — It is 
the vertical projection on the test platform 
of the point of intersection between the lateral 
axis of the articulating frame and the centre 
plane AB of the truck ( see also Fig. 19 ). 

d) For truck with a sprung castor wheel and 
a single unsprung drive ( steer ) wheel ( see 
Fig. 14) — It is the vertical projection on 
the test platform of the point of intersection 
Ix-tween the centreline of the drive wheel 
axle and the centreline of the drive wheel 
width, with the axle of the drive wheel 
positioned at right angles to the lilt axis.

g) For trucks with non-articulalcd, non-sprung

5.7 Test Procedure 

5.7.1 A tnick is placed on the test platform, which 
is initially maintained in horizontal position as per 
5,6 and successively tested in accordance with 
Table 1. 

5.7.2 In each of these tests, the lest platform shall 
be tilted slowly to the slope indicated in the tabic. 
The truck is considered stable, if it passes all tests 
without overturning. 

5.7.3 For the purpose of these tests, the stability limits 
is taken to Ix: the test platform slope value which, 
if increased, would produce complete overturning 
of the truck. 



5.7.4 It is permissible in lateral tests for one of the 
load wheels to lose contact with the test platform 
and it is acceptable for parts of the structure or other 
designed features to make contact with the test 
platform. 

6 STABIIJTY TESTS FOR TRUCKS WIIH 
AITACHMENTS 

6.1 Trucks fitted with attachments other than fork 
amis shall be subjected to the same stability tests, 
except in ca.ses where the attachment can bring the 
centre of gravity of the load out of the plane AB 
of the truck. 

6.2 For the verification of the vertical position of 
the mast, a reference point with a fixed relationship 
to the Centre of Gravity of the lest load, G ( see 
Fig. 1 ) shall be chosen. 

63 The test load shall be the specified load a I the 
specified load centre distance indicated for the 
attachment when used on the truck being 
tested. 

6.4 The forklift height specified for the tests shall 
l^ measured between the test platform surface and 
the underside of the load or the attachment, 
whichever is the lower. 



Standftrd Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the flwrfaw o/ /m/Za/j 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the 
producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity 
to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the 
use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained 
from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods
